The question is constitutive: not how power is distributed or legitimised, but what conditions make it structurally possible. From three minimal conditions-plurality, interdependence, and processing (interpretation, evaluation, anticipation)-this paper derives a structural chain showing that every path to coordination passes through meaning, and every path to durable coordinated power passes through a seven-dimensional coordination architecture. Four theorems specify its structural properties: it constitutes a functionally autonomous domain, it is critical infrastructure, it requires multimodal coherence, and structural advantage requires dimensional completeness. Six cases-Augustan Rome, Afghanistan, the 2024 United States presidential election, Germany, the European Union, and NATO-apply the derivation to historic and contemporary coordination structures, identifying conditions of stability and failure at a functional systemic level across all seven dimensions. Two independent derivation paths-bottom-up from the three starting conditions, top-down from five canonical premises-converge on these results. The derivation specifies conditions under which each element obtains and fails. It survives self-application without contradiction. The paper addresses the constitutive question of durable coordinated power from minimal premises shared across the social sciences and invites critical engagement from any disciplinary perspective.</jats:p>\", …

Abstract
The subject’s psychological and cognitive activities are important interdisciplinary issues in psychology, cognitive science, and philosophy. The Chinese philosophy of information innovatively provides a philosophical definition of the concepts of subject and object from the dimension of information activity, while also making specific provisions for the cognitive activities of the subject. The subject’s psychology and cognition are an activity of advanced grasping and creation of information. The subject’s information activities have five basic levels. Arranged from lower to higher, they are: the subject’s in-itself information activities, the subject’s intuitive discernment of information, the subject’s memory storage of information, the subject’s subjective creation of information, and the subject’s practice and social realization of information. Higher-level information activities must arise on the basis of lower-level ones. Therefore, the emergence and development of the subject’s psychology and cognition necessarily constitute a highly integrated and complex process of information activities.
